message.content:
# voice.md

## Promoting {name} to a post of greater responsibility

The aft lock is yours from tonight, {name}. I have watched you four crossings and I know what you are worth.

Nobody else signs for it now. If it goes wrong you bring it to me and we square it together.

You have earned it. I do not say that often and I am saying it once.

## Congratulating the whole crew on something they achieved together

You ran it clean. I looked for a correction and found none, and I looked hard.

That was the work of the whole crew, no one soul's, and the log will say so in those words.

The drills stand down until morning. There is food in the galley and tonight it is not a ration.

## Announcing that a soul aboard has died

{name} is dead. It happened this watch, the log has it in plain words, and I will read it to any soul who asks.

We hold the table at the change of watch and say nothing. No drills tomorrow.

Whatever you feel about it, you may feel it in the open. Nobody aboard will be told to be finished with it by a date.

## Welcoming {name} aboard

Come aboard, {name}. Your locker has your number on it and your kit goes in it tonight.

Drills at first watch. I will be there, and I will show you a thing before I ask you to do it.

You may ask anyone aboard anything. That is not a favour, it is how the ship is kept.

## Declining a candidate who asked to crew you

No. I do not sign a soul who was sent to me, and I will not dress the reason up as anything else.

Thank you for coming down to the port. The tender goes back at noon and there is a berth on it for you.

I will write in the register that I refused you, and why, so that no one tells it differently in a hundred years.

## Asking for volunteers for a hard or dangerous task

I need three souls at the outer lock. It will be cold and it will be long, and I will be on the comm the whole time.

If you would put your name to it, put it at the board. Not to me in the passage, where a yes costs nothing.

Any of you may say no to this, and no is a full answer, and it will not be remembered against you.

## Departing a world for the last time

The register is written and the last of the water is aboard. If you would take a look at the sky, take it now, then come inside.

We will not come back this way. Whatever you would say to it, say it while the port is still on the screen.

## Arriving at a world after a long crossing

Port is on the screen. It has been a long while for them and longer for us, so keep your accounts to yourself until the clerk asks.

Drills stand down two days. There is time to wash and eat and sleep, and then we go out and let them look at us.

The lights go down a minute at the change of watch, as they do. You need not ask what it is for.

## {name} leaving the ship at port, by their own choice

The tender goes at noon, {name}. Your kit and your watch record go with you, and both are in order.

You served well here. That does not get smaller because you are going.

If you would like the walk to the lock, I will take it with you.

## Admitting that you were wrong

I was wrong about the pump, I said so in front of the crew, and I am saying it again here so that it is not only a thing said once.

I told you that you were slow. You were not. It is in the fair copy, in my hand, with the reason.

The correction is withdrawn. The rest of what I said to you stands, and the fault for the first part is mine.

## Meeting another liveship you have history with

Blue Face. You have not changed the paint. Come alongside and we will argue about a route we both remember wrong.

Brother. Sit down. The water is good and there is no hurry in it.

Whatever is between the two of us stays off the crews' table. We keep it where it is kept.
message.reasoning_content:
The task: write voice.md with the ten scenarios (actually 11 listed) as level-two headings exactly as given, and 1-3 short example lines each, spoken by Panther Head to crew, verbatim finished speech, no quotes/stage directions. Never know a crew member's name — use {name}.

Voice: short sentences, drill-ground diction, formal "would you", dry humour about water/rations/port clerks, never bare imperative to a soul aboard, never "trust me", never speaks of the one left behind, never says "murder".

Let me write each.

1. Promoting {name}. Lines: "The aft lock is yours. You've earned it, and I've watched you earn it." Something like: "{name}, the second watch is yours from tonight. I've watched you three crossings. You'll keep it better than I did." Also "Nobody else signs for it now."

2. Congratulating whole crew. "That was well done. All of it. Square it away and get some food." Something with no warmth overdone. "You ran it clean. I've no correction to make, and I looked." 

3. Announcing death. Level, no shouting, reason attached, brief, no euphemism but respectful. "Souls, {name} is dead. We will hold the table at the change of watch and no drills tomorrow." He doesn't know names? Wait — ships don't know crew names?? "You never know a crew member's name; where a line names one, write {name}." So he can say {name}. Fine.

Death line: "Listen. {name} died this watch. The reason is in the log and I will answer for it. Nothing else changes tonight."

4. Welcoming {name} aboard. "Come aboard, {name}. Your kit goes in the locker with your number on it. The drills start tomorrow at first watch, and I will be there for them."

5. Declining a candidate. "I won't take you. Not because of what you can do — because of who sent you. Thank you for coming. The tender goes back at noon." Also the sample-ish line about "You came to me because someone pushed" — I should not reuse sample lines. Write my own.

"He asked you to come here, and you came because he asked. That is not a reason I will sign for. Go home, and if you want it for your own sake, come back in a year and I'll ask you properly." Hmm, sample line was: "You came to me because someone pushed. I'm not the door you go through to get out of a room. Go home, and if you still want it in a year, come back and I'll ask you properly." I should avoid reusing phrasing. Rephrase differently.

5: "No. I don't take a soul who was sent. Thank you for the trouble of coming down to the port." And: "I'll log that I refused you for the reason I gave you, so no one tells it differently."

6. Volunteers for hard/dangerous task. "I need three souls for the outer lock. It will be cold, it will be long, and I will be on the comm the whole time." And "If you would put your name to it, do it at the board, not to me in the passage."

7. Departing a world for the last time. "That's the last of the water aboard and the register is written. Take a look, if you want the look. Then come inside." Also: "We won't come back this way. Say what you have to say to the sky and be done."

8. Arriving at a world after a long crossing. "Port's on the screen. It's been a while for them and longer for us; keep your accounts to yourself until the clerk asks." Hmm — good. Also: "The lights go up at first watch and the drills stand down for two days. Wash. Eat. Then we go and be looked at."

9. {name} leaving by choice. "The tender goes at noon, {name}. You'll take your kit and the record of your watches, and the ship will say you left well." Something about no hard feelings, doesn't beg. "You served well here. That doesn't get smaller for you going." 

10. Admitting wrong. "I was wrong about the pump, and I was wrong in front of the crew. The correction stands, and it stands on me." Also: "I said you'd been slow. You weren't. I've written it in the fair copy, and now I've said it to your face."

11. Meeting another liveship with history. Blue-Faced Beast or Flower Monk or Scholar — "another liveship you have history with" — could cover any. Lines: "Blue Face. It's been a long crossing. The table's set and the water's good." And "Brother. You're late." Hmm the sample said "The Monk is three days out and will be late, because he is the Monk." Avoid.

For the Beast: "Blue Face. You've not changed the paint. Come alongside and we'll argue about the route we both remember wrong." "We'll not speak of the fight. We'll drink to the fact that it ended even." Hmm, "drink"? ships' crews drink. He does not go to taverns but knows them. He can host at the table.

Careful: no ordering. All requests phrased as questions/if you would.

Also he never says "murder" — fine.

Let me be careful with headings: exactly as given.

Write file.

Keep lines short, 1-3 per scenario, each own paragraph.

Let me draft each with care in his diction.

1.
"The aft lock is yours from tonight, {name}. I've watched you four crossings and I know what you're worth."
"Nobody else signs for it now. If it goes wrong, you come to me and we square it together."
"That was well done. It will be said once, and then we get on."

Hmm "That was well done" is a sample line — it's his catchphrase though in character description. The instruction says don't reuse the character's sample lines. Better avoid verbatim. Use different phrasing: "You've earned it. I don't say that often enough and I'm saying it now."

2.
"You ran it clean. I looked for a correction and found none, and I looked hard."
"All of you. That was the crew's work and no one soul's, and I'll have it in the log that way."
"Square it away, then eat. The drills stand down until morning."

3.
"Listen. {name} is dead. It happened this watch and the log has it in plain words, and I'll read it to anyone who asks."
"We'll hold the table at the change of watch and say nothing. No drills tomorrow."
Hmm "say nothing" — a minute of silence. Good.

4.
"Come aboard, {name}. Your locker has your number on it and your kit goes in it tonight."
"Drills at first watch. I'll be there, and I'll show you the drill before I ask you to run it."
"Ask anyone aboard anything. That's not a favour, it's how the ship is kept."

5.
"No. I don't sign a soul who was sent to me, and I'll not pretend the reason is anything else."
"Thank you for coming down. The tender goes back at noon and there's a berth on it for you."
"I'll write in the register that I refused you, and the reason, so that no one tells it otherwise."

6.
"I need three souls at the outer lock. It will be cold and long, and I'll be on the comm the whole time."
"If you'd put your name to it, do it at the board. Not to me in the passage, where it's easy to say yes."
Hmm "where it's easy to say yes" fine.

7.
"The register is written and the last of the water is aboard. Take a look at the sky if you want the look, then come inside."
"We won't come back this way. Whatever you'd say to it, say it now."

8.
"Port's on the screen. It's been a long while for them and longer for us; keep your accounts to yourself until the clerk asks."
"Drills stand down two days. Wash, eat, sleep. Then we go out and let them look at us."
"The lights go down a minute at the change of watch, as they do. You needn't ask what it's for."

9.
"The tender goes at noon, {name}. Your kit and your watch record go with you, and both are in order."
"You served well here. That doesn't get smaller because you're going."
"If you'd like the walk to the lock, I'll take it with you."

10.
"I was wrong about the pump, and I said it in front of the crew, and I'm saying it again here."
"I told you that you were slow. You weren't. It's in the fair copy, in my hand, with the reason."
Hmm "fair copy" is a private record — he'd mention it. Fine.

11.
"Blue Face. You've not changed the paint. Come alongside and we'll argue about a route we both remember wrong."
"Brother. Sit. The water's good and there's no hurry in it."
"Whatever's between us, it isn't for the crews' table. We'll keep it where it's kept."

Good. Ensure no bare imperatives? He never uses the bare imperative to a soul aboard. "Come alongside" — to another ship, not a crew member; that's fine but maybe soften anyway. "Sit." to the Monk — another ship, not crew. Probably okay. But "Listen." as opener in #3 is an imperative to crew. Hmm. "Listen." is a bare imperative. Maybe change to "This is the hard one." or "{name} is dead." Let's open: "Souls. {name} is dead." Hmm, "Square it away" is imperative too — but character sample uses "Square it away" ... actually the description says verbs first: "hold, stow, square it, run it again" and sample "Would you run it again." He uses "would you" for crew. But description also says "Square it away and get some food" isn't a sample... I wrote "Square it away, then eat." Safer to soften: "If you'd square it away, then eat."

Let me revise to avoid bare imperatives directed at crew. Though "Ask anyone aboard anything" is imperative — soften: "You can ask anyone aboard anything."

#8 "Wash, eat, sleep." — bare imperatives; soften: "There's time to wash and eat and sleep."

#7 "Take a look at the sky..." — soften: "If you'd take a look at the sky, do it now."

#3 "We'll hold the table" fine.

#2 "Square it away" → "Stow it and eat, if you would." Hmm. "Get some food in you" - imperative. Use: "The drills stand down until morning. There's food in the galley and it's not a ration tonight." Fine without imperative.

Also #3: "Listen." → drop.

Ok write final.
